extracted.intended_audience: NIH Scientific Review Group members and other peer reviewers of NIH grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Orientation and procedural guidance for reviewers who evaluate NIH grant applications, covering pre-meeting responsibilities, writing critiques, scoring, meeting discussion, voting, post-meeting edits, and ethical requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-meeting review assignments and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine your review assignments, review materials [including Funding Opportunity Announcements (FOAs) and applications], and instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review all applications pending review in the meeting for conflicts of interest or appearance of conflict; contact the SRO immediately if you perceive a conflict or have questions about assignment-expertise match.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest pre-review certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the 'NIH Conflict of Interest Rules: Information for Reviewers of NIH Applications and R&D Contract Proposals' and complete the NIH pre-review Certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you perceive a conflict, contact the SRO immediately. You must sign the post-review certification that you did not participate in any evaluation where you knowingly had a conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality certification and handling of materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Sign the Confidentiality Certification (usually in the Internet Assisted Review module).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All applications and related materials are privileged communications that cannot be shown to or discussed with unauthorized individuals; prohibited actions include sharing materials with non-designated individuals, granting access to secure systems, disclosing committee deliberations, and using application information for personal benefit. You must leave review materials with the SRO or destroy them at the conclusion of the review meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of critique templates and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Use critique templates provided by the SRO. Use bullets to note strengths and weaknesses for each of the scored review criteria and provide context and an explanation for your comments based on the project (e.g., refer to a Specific Aim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While brevity is acceptable, bullets should express complete thoughts and be sufficient to inform the reader. Download templates and enter bulleted comments directly; if composing elsewhere, paste as plain text to retain bullets. See Critique Template Instructions for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact paragraph requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a paragraph summarizing the factors that informed your Overall Impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph should be a stand-alone assessment of the strengths and weaknesses outlined for each of the scored criteria and additional review criteria, not a restatement or summary of the specific aims or the bulleted comments. Succinctly state the underlying rationale for the Overall Impact score. (For other activity codes overall impact may be defined differently.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Uploading critiques and scores to IAR
rubrics_metrics.description: Gain access to and upload critiques, preliminary overall impact scores and individual criterion scores to the Internet Assisted Review (IAR) site for the applications assigned to you; a deadline will be provided by the SRO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter scores into IAR (not on the template); read posted critiques for your assigned applications and other applications (access denied where you have a COI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring system — 9-point scale and whole numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH scoring system uses a 9-point scale for the overall impact score and individual scores for (at least) five scored criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratings are in whole numbers only (no decimal ratings). NIH expects that scores of 1 or 9 to be used less frequently than the other scores. 5 is considered an average score. For both types of score, ratings are whole numbers only. See the Scoring System and Procedure for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: No formula tying criterion scores to overall impact
rubrics_metrics.description: No formulas used to derive the overall impact score from the individual criterion scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh the different criteria as you see fit in deriving your overall scores. The Overall Impact score is not necessarily the average of the individual criterion scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score the application as presented
rubrics_metrics.description: Score an application as presented in its entirety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may not modify your scores on the assumption that a portion of the work proposed will be deleted or modified according to the SRG’s recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (primary evaluative dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overall impact score and critique to reflect your assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the five (or more) scored review criteria, and additional review criteria (as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic and applied research are equally relevant; evaluate overall impact in the context of the application. Unless stated otherwise in the FOA, an application does not need to be strong in all categories to be judged likely to have major scientific impact. Provide a paragraph summarizing the factors that informed your Overall Impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criteria — separate scoring required
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider each of the scored review criteria in the determination of scientific and technical merit and give a separate score for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most FOAs for Research Projects have the following five scored review criteria: Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach, and Environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (scored criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the importance of the problem or critical barrier to progress in the field that the project addresses and the potential of the project to improve scientific knowledge or clinical practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall Impact and Significance are different; Significance informs the likelihood of sustained, powerful influence but is not identical to Overall Impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s) (scored criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the qualifications and expertise of the members of the research team for the work proposed, including the Personal Statement in each Biosketch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless the application is for a fellowship or career development award, remarks about career tracks, titles, or salaries should be reserved for the Additional Comments to the Applicant box, or the Budget section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (scored criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the application challenges and seeks to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms through novel concepts, approaches, or methodologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovation is one of the scored criteria to be considered alongside the others when determining scientific and technical merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (scored criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses, including potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider rigor of methodology and whether the approach is appropriate to achieve the aims; reviewer guidance documents (e.g., Rigor and Transparency) provide additional considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment (scored criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the institutional support, equipment, and other physical resources available to the investigators that contribute to the probability of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environment is scored separately and contributes to the overall judgment of scientific and technical merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Criteria (no separate scores)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, consider the additional review criteria in the determination of scientific and technical merit and an overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not give separate scores for these items. Examples and guidance documents are provided for human subjects, vertebrate animals, inclusion, stem cells, etc.; program staff will administratively handle concerns on these items following the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Considerations (do not affect overall impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, comment on each of the additional review considerations, but do not assign scores and do not consider these items when determining an overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program staff will administratively handle any concerns on these items following the review. Examples include budget information and select agent considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting procedures and presentation responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The SRO will begin the meeting by reviewing policies and meeting procedures. Assigned reviewers will share their initial overall impact score and should be prepared to explain the significance of the proposed research and the overall impact the research will have on the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group discussion follows assigned reviewer presentations. Open discussion of scientific merit may result in disparate levels of enthusiasm; the reasons for disparities should be made clear to allow informed votes and a high-quality summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion of protections before final scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Because consideration of human subject protections, inclusion plans, vertebrate animals or biohazards can affect scientific and technical merit, these elements are discussed before final scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address these elements openly in discussion so their impact on merit and scoring is clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final scoring, voting eligibility, and mail reviewer handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Each discussed application is given a score by all reviewers who are eligible to vote on that application. Both regularly appointed and temporary members vote for applications for which they do not have a conflict of interest. Mail Reviewers do not attend the review meeting and their preliminary overall impact scores are not used to calculate the average preliminary or final score; their critiques and scores are considered by the review panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may use non-numeric impact scores (AB, CF, NP). The scores from all eligible reviewers for a given application are averaged (calculated to one decimal point) and multiplied by 10 to determine the final overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible non-numeric voting codes
rubrics_metrics.description: You may use non-numeric impact scores, as appropriate: AB – abstain from voting; CF – conflict of interest; did not participate in the discussion and scoring; NP – not present during discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other committee decision scenarios include ND - not discussed; NR - not recommended for further consideration; DF – deferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of outlier preliminary scores
rubrics_metrics.description: If a particular score is an outlier, the reviewer must have stated his/her concerns during the discussion so that they can be reflected in the final summary statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlier concerns should be articulated during the discussion to be captured in the summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-meeting edit phase and score/critiques revision
rubrics_metrics.description: After the meeting, the SRO sets an 'Edit Phase' in IAR. You should edit your criterion scores and critiques to reflect any changes to their preliminary assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make edits during the designated edit phase. You must sign your post-meeting Conflict of Interest (COI) certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest during meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: During the meeting, if you have a conflict of interest with any application or proposal, you must leave the room during evaluation and scoring of that application or proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alert the SRO immediately of any conflicts of which you are aware.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research misconduct policy for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Research misconduct is defined as fabrication, falsification, or plagiarism in proposing, performing, or reviewing research, or in reporting research results, but not honest error or differences of opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make allegations of potential misconduct in the critique or during the meeting discussion; instead, bring such concerns to the attention of the SRO in a confidential manner, preferably before the study section meets.
